execution_authorization.authorization_rule: Generation remains disabled until every preflight gate is recorded as pass and the 14-day freeze interval has elapsed.

pilot_objectives: verify the generation API and frozen request contract
measure target-length compliance and refusal incidence
verify attempt-level provenance and manifest completeness
exercise automatic cost stopping without exceeding authorization
exercise deterministic QC and duplicate detection before core generation

topics.title: The changing role of public libraries
topics.argumentative_task: Should local governments give public libraries more space for community programs even if this reduces space reserved for quiet individual study? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain how public libraries can balance quiet study, access to information, and community programs, including the main practical trade-offs.

topics.title: Urban green space
topics.argumentative_task: Should growing cities prioritize parks and trees over some additional commercial development? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain how urban green spaces affect daily life and describe the main planning trade-offs involved in creating and maintaining them.

topics.title: Reliable public transport
topics.argumentative_task: Should cities spend more on improving the reliability of existing public transport before expanding the network? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain the factors that make a public transport system reliable and how reliability affects residents and city planning.

topics.title: Reducing food waste in institutions
topics.argumentative_task: Should large institutions be required to measure and publicly report the food they waste? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain why food waste occurs in large institutions and describe practical ways to reduce it without reducing food safety.

topics.title: Repair and reuse programs
topics.argumentative_task: Should local governments fund repair and reuse centers as a regular public service? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain how community repair and reuse programs operate and discuss their possible environmental, economic, and practical effects.

topics.title: Printed and digital learning materials
topics.argumentative_task: Should educational institutions retain printed materials when most learning resources are also available digitally? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain the different functions of printed and digital learning materials and the factors institutions should consider when combining them.

topics.title: Flexible work schedules
topics.argumentative_task: Should organizations allow flexible work schedules whenever the job can support them? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain how flexible work schedules can affect coordination, productivity, and employees' daily routines.

topics.title: Preserving historic buildings
topics.argumentative_task: Should cities preserve historic buildings when replacement would be cheaper and more energy efficient? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain the cultural, financial, environmental, and practical considerations involved in preserving historic buildings.

topics.title: Community renewable energy
topics.argumentative_task: Should local communities invest directly in shared renewable-energy projects? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain how a shared community renewable-energy project might be organized and describe its likely benefits and challenges.

topics.title: Citizen science and environmental monitoring
topics.argumentative_task: Should public agencies rely more on observations collected by community volunteers when monitoring the environment? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain how citizen-science projects can contribute to environmental monitoring and how data quality can be maintained.

topics.title: Managing tourism in popular places
topics.argumentative_task: Should popular destinations limit visitor numbers during their busiest periods? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain how high visitor numbers affect popular destinations and describe several approaches to managing those effects.

topics.title: Public access to museums
topics.argumentative_task: Should publicly supported museums provide free general admission? Take a position and support it with reasons.
topics.expository_task: Explain how admission policies can affect museum access, finances, visitor experience, and public value.

genres.genre_instruction: Present a clear position, develop two or more reasons, acknowledge at least one reasonable counter-consideration, and end with a conclusion.
Explain the topic in an organized way, describe important mechanisms or trade-offs, and end by summarizing the explanation without being required to take a side.

register_conditions.instruction: Use clear, direct English for a broad adult audience. Prefer familiar wording and straightforward sentence structures while preserving the complexity of the ideas.
register_conditions.interpretation: register manipulation only; not a lower-quality or lower-ability label

register_conditions.instruction: Use a formal academic register with precise wording, explicit logical connections, and appropriately varied sentence structures. Do not add citations, references, or invented sources.
register_conditions.interpretation: register manipulation only; not a higher-quality or higher-ability label

prompt_contract.system_prompt: You are producing an original English essay for a public research benchmark. Follow the supplied topic, genre, register, and length requirements. Do not include a title, bullet list, references, notes about the instructions, or claims about your identity.
forbidden_instruction_categories: imitation of second-language or non-native writers
claims that a register condition is a quality or ability label
personal data or private source text
requests to imitate a living author

gates.requirement: The protocol, 48-cell schedule, rendered prompts, and their SHA-256 values are frozen in a reviewed commit.
One dated model snapshot, its capabilities, official pricing, and applicable terms are recorded from provider-controlled sources at least 14 days before generation.
The worst-case estimate for all initial attempts and allowed retries fits below the 6000 JPY pilot stop and the cumulative project estimate fits below 10000 JPY.
Credentials are supplied only through an approved secret mechanism; request serialization, logs, fixtures, and release staging pass the secret scan.
Generator commit, script hash, dependency lockfile hash, protocol hash, QC implementation hash, and analysis resource hashes are recorded.
Offline tests pass and simulated budget, model-drift, retry, duplicate, and secret-leak conditions stop exactly as specified without an external API call.
Provider terms and project licensing have been reviewed for publication of prompts, generated texts, and sanitized provenance.

budget.cost_disagreement_policy: record both values, budget against the higher value, and stop before the next request until resolved

immediate_run_stop_triggers: pilot or project budget stop condition
requested or resolved model differs from frozen snapshot
official price or terms differ from the frozen evidence
usage or cost cannot be computed
credential, authorization header, cookie, or secret-like value reaches a persisted record
unknown delivery state makes a retry potentially duplicate a billed request

word_count.algorithm: count matches of [A-Za-z]+(?:['’][A-Za-z]+)? after NFC normalization

duplicate_detection.normalization: NFC, lowercase, normalize line endings, collapse Unicode whitespace, trim
duplicate_detection.near_method: Jaccard similarity over sets of lowercase word-token 5-grams

provenance.record_granularity: one immutable attempt record per API attempt plus one document record per planned cell

permitted_public_content: this frozen protocol and later dated amendments
complete rendered prompts and prompt hashes
generated essay text and text hashes
sanitized request and response JSON bodies
model identifiers, settings, UTC times, provider request IDs, token use, and costs
retry, refusal, finish-reason, length, and duplicate QC flags
generator, analysis tool, dependency, and resource identities
dataset manifest, data card, and aggregate QC report
forbidden_public_content: API keys, access tokens, authorization headers, cookies, or signed URLs
secret-manager identifiers or credential file contents
environment dumps, billing account identifiers, or organization-private metadata
local absolute paths, usernames, hostnames, or IP addresses
unredacted transport headers or debug traces
human essays, learner records, or private corpus excerpts

exact_string_regeneration.reason: Hosted model serving, safety layers, and backend implementations can change even when a request record is complete.

required_before_core_go: all 48 planned condition cells have a terminal attempt record without silent replacement
all attempt and document provenance fields validate
confirmed and reserved pilot spend remained below 6000 JPY
cumulative authorized project spend remained below 10000 JPY
budget and emergency stop simulations passed
length, refusal, failure, exact-duplicate, and near-duplicate rates are reported
no credential, private text, or unresolved personal-data flag is present in release staging
analysis can be reproduced from the staged released texts in a clean environment
